title: Spanner Omni Reaches GA, Replacing Google's Atomic Clocks and File System with Software
gist: Google made Spanner Omni, a deploy-anywhere version of Spanner, generally available by replacing Colossus and TrueTime with software; it ships without an availability SLA, shifting operational burden to customers, and supports vector search and MCP for agents.

insights.claim: Spanner Omni replaces Colossus with a Colossus-like abstraction over local file systems and TrueTime with software error-bounded time sync, which Google says performs comparably to the managed service for most workloads.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Google's globally consistent database is no longer tied to Google hardware, opening on-prem and multicloud markets.

insights.claim: Software time sync works because Spanner overlaps uncertainty waits with other work, so it tolerates weaker bounds than TrueTime provides in practice.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Atomic-clock hardware may not be required for strong consistency databases.
insights.locator: Google's explanation for why that works

insights.claim: Paxos, automatic sharding and synchronous replication carry over unchanged, with Google's internal benchmarks claiming millions of queries per second across petabytes in a single region.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers

insights.claim: Google offers no availability SLA for Spanner Omni because it runs on customer-managed infrastructure, offering reference topologies instead.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Lack of SLA limits suitability for risk-averse enterprises versus managed Spanner.
insights.locator: Google does not provide availability SLAs

insights.claim: A CTO argues the shift is operational not architectural: failure domains, patching and upgrades, backup, key management and audit become the customer's responsibility.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Total cost should be priced in ops toil, not features.
insights.quote: The interesting shift is operational, not architectural: once the same engine runs in your racks, the failure domains become yours.

insights.claim: The article recommends a like-for-like pilot of Omni versus managed Spanner measured on tail latency and ops toil.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Evaluate on tail latency and ops toil rather than feature parity.
insights.quote: A like-for-like pilot against the managed service, measured on tail latency and ops toil instead of feature parity

insights.claim: Google Cloud-dependent integrations such as BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog and Gemini Enterprise are excluded, and the docs name Google Cloud and Amazon but not Azure as supported public clouds.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Omni weakens lock-in to Google ecosystem but not Google data-stack stickiness; Azure absence is a gap.

insights.claim: Spanner Omni supports GoogleSQL, PostgreSQL and graph query languages with vector, full-text and columnar models, and MCP Toolbox lets agents use it as an operational memory layer.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Databases are positioning as agent memory layers.
insights.locator: What does carry over is the database itself

insights.claim: Developer Edition is free for non-production with a 90-day license; Commercial Edition is a vCPU-based annual subscription with no published price.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers

insights.claim: Mercado Libre said Spanner Omni enables cross-cloud resilience against insider threats, ransomware and cloud outages that would be more complex with other providers.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Resilience and sovereignty, not performance, drive early adoption.
insights.locator: Mercado Libre, which built an internal developer gateway
